therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: dietary supplementation to alter tissue fatty acid composition
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: modulation of inflammatory mediators and cellular proliferation/apoptosis pathways
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients with stage I-III breast cancer
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: PUFA levels in normal and malignant breast tissue, plasma, and red blood cells

results.effect_size: Variable changes in PUFA levels across tissue types - omega-3 group showed increased EPA (20:5 n-3) in plasma (+35,551 vs +2,291 ug/ml) and RBC (+15,066 vs -1,187 ug/ml)
results.target_engagement_evidence: Omega-3 supplementation increased EPA and DHA levels in plasma and red blood cells, demonstrating target engagement
biomarker_changes: Increased EPA (20:5 n-3) in plasma and RBC in omega-3 group
Increased DHA (22:6 n-3) in plasma and RBC in omega-3 group
Higher PGE2 and PGD2 levels in malignant tissue in omega-3 group
Improved n-3/n-6 ratio in plasma in omega-3 group
subgroup_findings: Different PUFA incorporation patterns between normal and malignant breast tissue
Metabolite profiles differed between tissue types
